name: islam
followers: about 2 billion, the second largest religion
founder: the prophet muhammad, the last in a line of prophets going back to adam
scriptures: the quran; the hadith, reports of the prophet's words and deeds
places: mecca and the kaaba, medina, and jerusalem
summary: submission (islam) to the one god, allah, as revealed in the quran to the prophet muhammad. muslims see it as the same faith taught by every prophet from adam, through abraham, moses, and jesus, to muhammad.
creation: god created the heavens and the earth in six days, commanding "be", and it was. he made adam from clay, breathed his spirit into him, and made him his deputy on earth.
age: the quran gives no date. many scholars note that a "day" with god can be like a thousand or fifty thousand years, and many muslims accept the scientific age. the islamic calendar counts years from the hijra in 622 ce.

events.text: god alone exists. he creates the heavens and the earth in six days, saying "be", and it is. he makes the angels from light and the jinn from smokeless fire
god shapes adam from clay, breathes his spirit into him, and teaches him the names of all things. he tells the angels to bow to adam; iblis refuses in pride and is cast out
adam and hawwa (eve) eat from the forbidden tree. they repent and god forgives them, then sends them down to earth, where adam becomes the first prophet
the prophet nuh (noah) calls his people to god for 950 years; the unbelievers drown in the flood and the ark comes to rest on mount judi
ibrahim (abraham) breaks his people's idols and is thrown into a fire that god makes cool. with his son ismail he builds the kaaba in mecca, the first house for the worship of the one god
musa (moses) confronts pharaoh, leads the children of israel to freedom, and receives the tawrat (torah)
dawud (david) receives the zabur (psalms); his son sulayman (solomon) rules with wisdom and can speak with birds, animals, and jinn
isa (jesus) is born by a miracle to the virgin maryam. he is a prophet who receives the injil (gospel); muslims believe he was not crucified but raised up to god
muhammad is born in mecca, into the clan of hashim of the quraysh tribe; he is orphaned young
muhammad, a trusted merchant, marries khadija, a widow who runs her own trading business
in the cave of hira, the angel jibril (gabriel) brings muhammad the first verses of the quran: "read, in the name of your lord who created"
muhammad begins preaching in public; the leaders of mecca turn against him and his followers are persecuted
the night journey: muhammad is carried to jerusalem and rises through the heavens; the five daily prayers are given
the hijra: muhammad and his followers move to medina. the islamic calendar counts its years from here
the muslims defeat a much larger meccan army at the battle of badr
mecca surrenders; muhammad clears the idols from the kaaba
muhammad makes his farewell pilgrimage and dies in medina; abu bakr becomes the first caliph
the caliph uthman sends out standard copies of the quran to the main cities of the growing empire
the first civil war among muslims; ali, the fourth caliph, is assassinated in 661
husayn, grandson of the prophet, is killed at karbala; the division between sunni and shia deepens
the dome of the rock is built in jerusalem
the abbasids found baghdad, soon home to the house of wisdom and a golden age of learning
al-bukhari completes his collection of hadith, which sunni muslims regard as the most reliable after the quran
al-ghazali writes the revival of the religious sciences, bringing law, theology, and sufi devotion together
the mongols sack baghdad and kill the last abbasid caliph there
mansa musa of mali makes his pilgrimage to mecca, showing the islamic world the wealth of west africa
the ruler of malacca becomes muslim; islam spreads through the trading ports of southeast asia
the ottomans take constantinople; the hagia sophia becomes a mosque
the new republic of turkey abolishes the ottoman caliphate
about one person in four is muslim; the largest muslim country is indonesia, and most muslims are not arabs
at the hour known only to god, the dead will rise and every soul will be judged; the righteous enter paradise

people.name: adam
people.about: made by god from clay and taught the names of all things; he repented and was forgiven

people.name: nuh
people.about: called his people to god for centuries and was saved from the flood in the ark

people.name: ibrahim
people.about: turned from idols to the one god and built the kaaba with his son ismail; the hajj retraces his family's story

people.name: ismail
people.about: the son whom ibrahim was ready to sacrifice, remembered at eid al-adha; ancestor of the arabs of mecca

people.name: musa
people.about: the prophet named most often in the quran; he spoke with god and received the tawrat

people.name: maryam
people.about: the only woman named in the quran, which has a chapter called by her name

people.name: isa
people.about: born of a virgin and given the injil; muslims believe he will return before the last day

people.name: khadija
people.about: a successful merchant and the first person to accept islam

people.name: muhammad
people.about: received the quran over 23 years and united arabia under islam; muslims call him the seal of the prophets

people.name: abu bakr
people.about: the prophet's closest friend, who led the community after his death

people.name: umar
people.about: led the conquests of syria, egypt, and persia and set up the islamic calendar

people.name: ali ibn abi talib
people.role: cousin and son-in-law of muhammad, the fourth caliph
people.about: shia muslims regard him as the first imam and the prophet's rightful successor

people.name: fatima
people.about: wife of ali and mother of hasan and husayn, deeply honored by all muslims

people.name: aisha
people.about: one of the most important sources of hadith and a teacher of the early community

people.name: husayn ibn ali
people.about: killed at karbala; his death is mourned every year by shia muslims on ashura

people.name: rabia of basra
people.about: taught that god should be loved for himself alone, not from fear of hell or hope of paradise

people.name: al-bukhari
people.about: is said to have checked some 600,000 reports to choose about 7,000 for his collection

people.name: al-ghazali
people.about: left a famous teaching post in baghdad in a spiritual crisis and later wrote the revival of the religious sciences

people.name: rumi
people.about: his poems of love for god are read around the world; his followers became the whirling dervishes

people.name: mansa musa
people.about: built mosques and schools in timbuktu after his famous pilgrimage

people.name: ibn battuta
people.about: journeyed across the islamic world from morocco to china and wrote about it

glossary.definition: the arabic word for god, used by arab christians and jews as well as muslims.
"successor": the leader of the muslim community after muhammad.
a festival: eid al-fitr at the end of ramadan, and eid al-adha at the time of the hajj.
the five duties of every muslim: the shahada, prayer (salah), charity (zakat), fasting in ramadan, and the hajj.
a report of something the prophet said or did, passed down through a chain of named people.
the pilgrimage to mecca, which every muslim who is able should make once in their life.
the move of muhammad and his followers from mecca to medina in 622, year 1 of the islamic calendar.
one who leads prayer; for shia muslims, the divinely guided leaders descended from ali.
beings made of smokeless fire, with free will like humans, mostly unseen.
the cube-shaped shrine at the center of the great mosque of mecca, which muslims face when they pray.
a muslim place of prayer, in arabic masjid, "place of bowing down".
a messenger of god. the quran names 25, from adam to muhammad, the last.
"the recitation": the holy book of islam, which muslims believe is the word of god revealed to muhammad in arabic.
the ninth month of the islamic year, when muslims fast from dawn to sunset.
the ritual prayer, said five times a day facing mecca.
the declaration of faith: "there is no god but god, and muhammad is the messenger of god."
"the way": islamic law and ethics, worked out by scholars from the quran and sunnah.
the second largest branch of islam, about a tenth to an eighth of muslims, who follow the line of ali and the imams.
the mystical path in islam, seeking closeness to god through prayer, remembrance, music, and poetry.
the example of the prophet's words and life, known from the hadith.
the largest branch of islam, followed by most muslims, who accept the first four caliphs in order.
the worldwide community of all muslims.
the yearly giving of a share of one's wealth to the poor and needy.
